versions.name: RXV2-0.9.686-log-colour
versions.notes: The Receiver log button at the foot of Black box was grey, which reads as disabled. It is now the Receiver log's own blue - bright, and clear of the green above it. Includes 0.9.685.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.685-button-gap
versions.notes: Read black box: the two buttons touched - the link above had no bottom margin and the button below had none at all. Checked by screenshot this time, not by reading the CSS. Includes 0.9.684.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.684-read-black-box
versions.notes: The Vibration check is now called READ BLACK BOX, because that is what it does - it grew from filter advice into the whole flight - and it lives inside the black box area instead of as a separate entry in the list. Black box (Flight recorder) leads with it, and the Receiver log sits at the foot of the same page, so everything about recordings is in one place. Includes 0.9.683.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.683-log-under-blackbox
versions.notes: The Receiver log is offered plainly at the foot of Black box (Flight recorder) - no heading, no explaining - and is off the front page. It reappears on the front page only for a receiver with no Rotorflight, which would otherwise have no Black box page to reach it through. Includes 0.9.682.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.682-receiver-log
versions.notes: Two things were both called the black box. The receiver's own is now the RECEIVER LOG - what this receiver saw: live status, the radio link, past flights and events - on the front page, in its title and help, and in search. Black box (Flight recorder) keeps that name for the flight controller's recording, and now carries a 'Not this one?' card pointing across to the Receiver log; the Receiver log points back. Includes 0.9.681.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.681-black-box
versions.notes: Rotorflight's Flight recorder is now called Black box (Flight recorder), and sits under B in the a-la-carte list where you look for it. The page, its help and everything that points at it say Black box; the search index keeps both meanings apart, since the receiver has a Black box page of its own. Includes 0.9.680.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.680-cli-leave
versions.notes: Command line: Leave without saving now leaves - it closes the session and then goes where the back arrow goes, instead of leaving you on a dead page to press Back yourself. Both buttons are disabled once the session is closed, which is what printed 'the command line was not open' when they were pressed again. Save and restart deliberately stays, because the flight controller is restarting and the message says so. Includes 0.9.679.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.679-help-links
versions.notes: Where a help screen tells you to use another page, it now offers it: the Filters help has Vibration check and Flight recorder buttons, and In-flight adjustments links the Switches page where the bank switch is set. Includes 0.9.678.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.678-ports-link
versions.notes: Before you start, step 2 now has an Open Ports button, so the one page it tells you to use is one tap away instead of something to go and find. Includes 0.9.677.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.677-cable-part
versions.notes: The help now names the exact cable: a Chenyang CY-UC-088-0.07M, 70 mm, flat, USB-C at both ends with both plugs right-angled, USB 2.0 data, 65 W, on Amazon. Any short one will do so long as it carries data. The website says the same and carries the photo of it fitted. Includes 0.9.676.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.676-cable-advice
versions.notes: Cable advice matches what actually works on the model: the shortest cable you can get, right-angled at BOTH ends if possible, tied down and left in - it costs nothing in the air because the receiver stops talking over USB the moment the radio link is live. Said in the Ways-to-connect footer, the Rotorflight menu help and Setup's USB socket bullet; the website carries the fitted photo. Includes 0.9.675.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.675-help-round
versions.notes: The help back button really is the round arrow now. 0.9.674 gave it the class the wide green Got-it button uses, and since that rule comes later in the stylesheet it won on every shared property - so it rendered as a full-width teal bar. It now has its own class, declared after, and the panel starts below it exactly as a page's content starts below its floating buttons (the button is 3em of its own 1.55em font, so 4.65em tall, not 3em). Verified by screenshot in a headless browser, not by reading the CSS. Includes 0.9.674.
